latest_release.name: v3.1.0
latest_release.body:
## What's Changed

Howdy! Today, I'm starting a new tradition for Harper. Instead of the bland, colorless release notes you've _been_ receiving for past releases, you'll now be getting these new, awesome release notes I type up myself. 

The hope is that by writing these notes directly, in addition to the updates on [my blog](https://elijahpotter.dev/), I can get closer to you guys, the people using Harper. I'll share some of the things on my mind, the places Harper is going, and the wonderful work Harper's community has gotten done since the last release.

We have a ton of updates and bug fixes coming in this release. I'll cover some of my favorite changes, but I won't be able to cover everything. You can find a list of ALL the changes in the PR notes at the end.

First off, we've simplified some parts of Harper's UI. In the desktop app, instead of seeing a green or red bar to signify if Harper is activated, you should see a dot below the Harper logo in the menu if the service is running. If the service is _not_ running, there's no dot. Simple enough. You'll also observe that the menu bar should look much nicer in both light and dark modes. In the Chrome Extension, we've reverted some of the changes from `v3.0.0` that made the popup menu (what you get when you click on the Harper logo) more "exciting". They were distracting and a little confusing, so we banished them.

Secondly, I've done a ton of work fixing bugs in our support for Google Docs. You should now see correct behavior when Harper checks sentences that span multiple pages and tables should now play more nicely with suggestions. Plus, thanks to @mvanhorn, we have some improved support for editors like WordPress' Gutenberg.

In the desktop app, we're pushing out some similar improvements. We got some reports that Harper didn't play well with setups with multiple monitors. It should be much cleaner now.

We also got some feedback that the Desktop app was a little confusing. We heard similar feedback a while ago about the Chrome Extension, which we addressed with a tip system. We set a similar "tip" system up for the Desktop app. We shall see if it help make things a little less confusing. From now on, you'll occasionally see tips appear when you review a highlighted problem in your text. 

The most important changes, as always, were in our core grammar engine. We've added a ton of new rules and fixed a number of broken ones. Thanks to everyone who opened PRs in that vein, especially @hippietrail who's been reviewing them so prodigiously.

I'll talk to you again in the next release! Thanks for using Harper. Have a great weekend.

Best, Elijah Potter (@elijah-potter)

### The PRs We Merged

* feat: kids-friendly → kid-friendly by @hippietrail in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4706
* fix(web): icons in the FAQ section looked weird by @elijah-potter in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4668
* feat(web): add time-series graph to the dashboard for reported lint frequency by @elijah-potter in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4712
* feat: redundant 'my first half of my life' etc. by @hippietrail in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4684
* feat: accuse as → accuse of by @hippietrail in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4700
* feat: tent to → tend to by @hippietrail in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4701
* fix(chrome-ext): remove distracting visual elements from the popup by @elijah-potter in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4713
* fix(ls): avoid config/doc_state lock-order deadlock by @willismonroe in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4711
* fix(core): don't flag a compound noun followed by a modal verb by @ozenyunus35 in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4630
* feat(core): flag "tenant" where "tenet" is meant by @manduinca in https://github.com/Automattic/harper/pull/4425
* fix(lint-framework): don't mistake a foreign element for the highlight style by @braklo in

Harper

[![Harper Binaries](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/binaries.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/binaries.yml) [![Website](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/build_web.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/build_web.yml) [![Checks](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/just_checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/automattic/harper/actions/workflows/just_checks.yml) [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/harper-ls)](https://crates.io/crates/harper-ls) ![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/harper.js) ![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/automattic/harper/total?label=Binary+Downloads) ![Obsidian Plugin Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/automattic/harper-obsidian-plugin/total?label=Obsidian+Plugin+Downloads) Harper is an English grammar checker designed to be _just right._ I created it after years of dealing with the shortcomings of the competition. Grammarly was too expensive and too overbearing. Its suggestions lacked context, and were often just plain _wrong_. Not to mention: it's a privacy nightmare. Everything you write with Grammarly is sent to their servers. Their privacy policy claims they don't sell the data, but that doesn't mean they don't use it to train large language models and god knows what else. Not only that, but the round-trip-time of the network request makes revising your work all the more tedious. LanguageTool is great, if you have gigabytes of RAM to spare and are willing to download the ~16GB n-gram dataset. Besides the memory requirements, I found LanguageTool too slow: it would take several seconds to lint even a moderate-size document. That's why I created Harper: it is the grammar checker that fits my needs. Not only does it take milliseconds to lint a document, take less than 1/50th of LanguageTool's memory footprint, but it is also completely private. Harper is even small enough to load via [WebAssembly.](https://writewithharper.com) ## Language Support Harper currently only supports English, but the core is extensible to support other languages, so we welcome contributions that allow for other language support. ## Performance Issues We consider long lint times bugs. If you encounter any significant performance issues, please create an issue on the topic. If you find a fix to any performance issue, we would appreciate the contribution. Just please make sure to read [our contribution guidelines first.](https://writewithharper.com/docs/contributors/introduction) ## Links - [Frequently Asked Questions](https://writewithharper.com/#faqs) - [Obsidian Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/obsidian) - [`harper-ls` Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/language-server) - Supported Editors' Documentation - [Visual Studio Code](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/visual-studio-code) - [Neovim](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/neovim) - [Helix](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/helix) - [Emacs](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/emacs) - [Zed](https://writewithharper.com/docs/integrations/zed) - [`harper.js` Documentation](https://writewithharper.com/docs/harperjs/introduction) - [Official Discord Server](https://discord.com/invite/JBqcAaKrzQ) ## Huge Thanks This project would not be possible without the hard work from those who [contribute](https://writewithharper.com/docs/contributors/introduction). Harper's logo was designed by [Lukas Werner](https://lukaswerner.com/).
